endpoint: POST /x402/<tool> — the paid x402 HTTP routes' REJECTION contract
why: This wave ADDED one error variant (invalid_content_type) to an existing public endpoint. Per CLAUDE.md, a new or modified public endpoint ships a shape snapshot with a drift check. No success-shape key changed; no existing error was removed or renamed.
allowed_keys_note: The union of keys across the three REJECTION shapes below — this snapshot governs the error contract. A 200 returns the core tool handler's existing public output verbatim (byte-parity with the MCP tool), which varies per tool and is snapshotted per tool elsewhere.

402.when: unpaid, cross-tool/underpaid proof, or a replayed nonce
402.note_w3: X402_CLAIM_UNAVAILABLE now shares the 402 status with X402_PAYMENT_REPLAY. A caller MUST branch on `code`, not on the status, to decide whether to retry: REPLAY is terminal, CLAIM_UNAVAILABLE is retryable and consumed nothing.

400 invalid_input.when: body parsed but failed the published JSON Schema for the tool

400 invalid_content_type.when: The caller DECLARED a body (content-length > 0) but it arrived empty because express.json() declined to parse it — a duplicated/comma-joined content-type, a missing content-type, or a non-JSON media type. Distinguishes a dropped body from a genuinely invalid one, which previously surfaced as a misleading JSON-Schema error AFTER the payment had already verified.
400 invalid_content_type.amended_by: OPS-X402-TRADE-CALL-CONTENT-TYPE-W1 (2026-07-29) — this check now runs BEFORE, and INDEPENDENTLY OF, schema validation. It was previously nested inside the validation-failure branch, so it only fired on routes whose schema has a REQUIRED field. On scan_funding_arb, scan_trade_calls and get_equity_regime every field is optional, so an unparsed body validated clean as {} and the route served a DEFAULTS-ONLY result and CHARGED for it, silently discarding the caller's parameters. All 7 payable routes now behave identically.
guarantees: Emitted ONLY on the paid path (tier==='x402' with a pendingSettlement); an unpaid request still 402s before validation, so the CDP Bazaar crawler contract is untouched (verified live: unpaid POST with a duplicated content-type returns 402, not 400).
No settlement is attempted: this branch precedes tryClaimPayment() and settleX402Async(), so the caller is not charged and no nonce is claimed.
Never fires when the content-type is a clean JSON media type — a genuinely empty body still returns invalid_input.
Uniform across ALL payable routes regardless of whether their JSON Schema has required fields — a paid request can never be served a defaults-only result built from a body that never parsed.

402 claim_unavailable.when: The claim store could not be reached or errored, so the server could NOT DETERMINE whether this payment proof had already been used. Distinct from a replay: a replay is a settled fact, this is an absence of knowledge.
402 claim_unavailable.guarantees: The payment proof was NOT consumed and NOT settled — the nonce remains spendable, so a retry costs the buyer nothing. The server refuses rather than serving, because a double-settle is an irreversible on-chain USDC charge plus a manual refund, whereas a refused call is a foregone sale.
402 claim_unavailable.why_402_not_5xx: Evaluated and DECIDED to keep 402 (OPS-ZERO-VS-UNKNOWN-W3). The consumers recorded on this snapshot do not branch on status: Circle Gateway's GatewayClient.pay() surfaces the body's `error` field verbatim, and the CDP buyers treat any 402 as the paywall. Changing the status is a strictly larger wire change than adding a code, and would move this response out of the branch those clients already handle. The retry signal is therefore carried by `code` + `retryable`, which is what a client must read anyway to distinguish this from X402_PAYMENT_REPLAY.

500 handler_error.when: An unhandled exception inside the x402 route handler.
500 handler_error.guarantees: Static message only — SEC-50 removed the raw err.message from this body; the real error is logged server-side. Says nothing about payment state.
500 handler_error.added_by: OPS-AUDIT-REMEDIATION-LOW-W1 shipped this code but never declared it here. Found 2026-08-05 by OPS-ZERO-VS-UNKNOWN-W3's new assertion that every code the route can emit is snapshot-declared — a pre-existing undeclared wire code, not a regression of this wave.

cache_contract.note: Paid routes are computed on demand and are never cached; rejection responses carry no cache headers.

consumers: Circle Gateway buyers via @circle-fin/x402-batching GatewayClient.pay() (surfaces the body's `error` field verbatim in its thrown message)
CDP x402 buyers via @x402/fetch and the CDP Bazaar crawler (unpaid GET/POST -> 402 only)
scripts/build-knowledge-json.mjs (projects this file into the public knowledge bundle's response_shapes)
drift_check_command: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST https://api.algovault.com/x402/get_market_regime -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'   # expect 402 (unpaid short-circuits before validation; a 400 here would mean the paywall stopped preceding the body check)
regression_tests: tests/x402-paid-path.test.ts — 'paid request whose content-type prevents body parsing' (drives the real mounted route over real fetch with a combined content-type)
tests/x402-rejection-diagnostics.test.ts — explainDroppedBody() predicate + its false-positive guards
